title: Correct acceleration calculation
description: Essential: The response must compute the acceleration during pulling as a = (F - μmg)/m, yielding 1 m/s².

title: Correct displacement under force
description: Essential: The response must compute the displacement in the first 5 seconds using x₁ = ½at², yielding 12.5 m.

title: Correct final velocity at 5s
description: Important: The response must determine the velocity at t=5s as v = at, yielding 5 m/s, before analyzing post-force motion.

title: Correct deceleration after force removal
description: Important: The response must compute the deceleration due to friction alone as a₂ = μg, yielding 2 m/s².

title: Correct additional displacement
description: Essential: The response must compute the additional displacement after force removal using x₂ = v²/(2a₂), yielding 6.25 m.

title: Newton's second law application
description: Important: The response must apply Newton's second law separately for the pulling and coasting phases.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The response should maintain consistent units (m, s, m/s²) throughout calculations.

title: Sign error in friction
description: Pitfall: Penalize if friction force is added to pulling force instead of subtracted when computing initial acceleration.

title: Ignoring friction after force removal
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the object is assumed to continue at constant velocity after force removal, neglecting deceleration.
